implementation.ordering: SeqCst fences under the existing exclusive Engine/VM lease
implementation.synchronized_methods: Engine.call wraps ACC_SYNCHRONIZED entry around the body/native path; static uses the declaring canonical Class object and instance uses receiver; normal, exception and structured-error returns release exactly one acquisition.
implementation.gc: Held object keys are VM roots until the last exit. Unheld monitor metadata is removed.
implementation.wait_set: Object wait/notify/notifyAll remain explicitly unavailable for an owner and do not release/mutate the lock; calls without ownership throw IllegalMonitorStateException.
implementation.entry: Free monitor acquisition or same-owner reentry; cross-owner contention fails API_UNAVAILABLE without changing owner/depth.
implementation.device_binding: Session.current_thread_id returns existing as_jni_thread/threadGetCurHandle; no synthetic Java Thread object is introduced.
implementation.dex_declaration_marker: ACC_DECLARED_SYNCHRONIZED (0x20000) is not treated as the execution-lock bit; D8 non-native synchronized methods execute their explicit monitor bytecode.
implementation.legacy_std: Existing std opcode behavior remains unchanged; new ownership code is selected only for the portable build.
implementation.identity: No NativeHost means the single interpreter owner; a bound backend must return a nonzero actual current_thread_id, otherwise API_UNAVAILABLE. Native and interpreter owners have distinct namespaces.
implementation.ownership: Held monitors map each heap object to owner identity and recursion depth. No zero-work monitor success.
implementation.exit: Only the owner can decrement; zero depth removes the record; unowned/wrong-owner exit throws IllegalMonitorStateException; null throws NullPointerException.

limitations: Blocking contention, wait-set scheduling, interrupt/timeout wakeup and Java Thread scheduling are not implemented.
Host native-provider identity tests intentionally switch a controlled identity token; they do not claim simultaneous OS-thread or Horizon execution.

Structured VM abort from an explicit synchronized block bypasses Java exception handlers; the engine must be disposed after such a fatal error. Synchronized method wrappers release on those returned errors.
Held monitors of a terminated native thread are not automatically reassigned; thread lifecycle monitor integration is outside this subset.
JNI MonitorEnter/MonitorExit slots are not newly implemented by this change.
No game first-screen or GPU claim follows from these host tests.
